## Metabolic Pathway Analysis

I used MinPath to infer potential metabolic pathways from enzyme annotations generated by Prokka.

### Initial analysis

I first analyzed `metabat.5` using its predicted enzyme commission (EC) numbers.

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/minpath

cat ../prokka/metabat.5/metabat.5.tsv | awk -F '\t' '$5{OFS="\t";print $1,$5}' | grep -v '^locus' > metabat.5.ec

minpath -ec metabat.5.ec -report metabat.5.ec.report -details metabat.5.ec.details
```

### Results and Interpretation

The input contained 515 gene–enzyme annotation records.

MinPath generated a report containing 438 lines, of which
221 were marked `minpath 1`, indicating pathways selected by
the algorithm.

These pathway predictions provide insight into potential
microbial metabolic capabilities. However, predicted pathways
do not establish that the corresponding metabolic processes
are active in the environment.

Further analysis will compare pathways associated with
photosynthesis and sulfur metabolism across the recovered
genome bins.

### Photosynthesis and Sulfur-Related Pathways

For `metabat.5`, MinPath selected several pathways associated with sulfur-containing compounds, including iron–sulfur cluster biosynthesis, sulfur volatiles biosynthesis, and chondroitin sulfate degradation.

A C4 photosynthetic carbon assimilation pathway was also selected. However, these predictions do not independently confirm photosynthetic activity or sulfur-based energy metabolism, as individual enzymes can participate in multiple biological pathways.

Further comparisons between genome bins are needed to assess how these potential metabolic functions are distributed across the black band disease-associated microbial community.

### Comparison Between Genome Bins

I compared the MinPath predictions for `metabat.5` and
`contig_328` to investigate potential differences in metabolism.

`metabat.5` contained 515 enzyme annotation records and
221 pathways selected by MinPath, while `contig_328` contained
920 annotation records and 339 selected pathways.

Both genomes had predictions associated with iron–sulfur cluster
biosynthesis, sulfur volatiles biosynthesis, chondroitin sulfate
degradation, and C4 carbon assimilation.

`contig_328` additionally showed predicted pathways associated
with assimilatory sulfate reduction and alternative C4 carbon
assimilation mechanisms.

These differences suggest variation in the metabolic potential
of the recovered bacteria. However, pathway predictions are
based on annotated genes and do not confirm active metabolism.


### Comparison Across All Genome Bins

I completed MinPath analysis for all 14 selected genome candidates using enzyme annotations generated by Prokka.

```{r pathway-summary}
pathway_summary <- data.frame(
  Genome = c(
    "metabat.26", "contig_328", "metabat.5",
    "metabat.35", "metabat.29", "metabat.40",
    "metabat.10", "metabat.38", "metabat.28",
    "metabat.51", "metabat.3", "metabat.62",
    "metabat.16", "metabat.47"
  ),
  Selected_Pathways = c(
    378, 339, 221, 163, 132, 106, 102,
    80, 74, 63, 59, 46, 43, 38
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  pathway_summary,
  col.names = c("Genome Bin", "Selected MinPath Pathways")
)
```

### Overall Interpretation

The number of predicted metabolic pathways varied considerably among the 14 genome candidates, ranging from 38 to 378.

`metabat.26`, classified within the cyanobacterial genus *Roseofilum*, had the greatest number of selected pathway predictions (378), followed by `contig_328` (339).

These results suggest variation in the predicted metabolic potential of the recovered bacterial genomes. However, differences in genome completeness and annotation coverage may influence the number of pathways detected.

The identification of sulfur-related metabolic pathways is relevant to understanding the complex microbial community associated with black band disease. Nevertheless, gene-based pathway predictions cannot independently establish metabolic activity or an organism's contribution to disease progression.
